subject: MCDS Warning: detection greater than one

messages.author: 010fa11e67a0d0b7
messages.subject: MCDS Warning: detection greater than one
parts:
Dear Distance users,

I am running a MCDS model with half-normal function and poisson distribution of observations. I set it up to estimate a global detection probability
and calculate abundance per strata. After the model runs I receive the following watrning messege:

 Maximum probability of detection is greater than one: invalid model fitted


I get a glogal detection probability of 0.74. However,  the programm still calculates a detection probability per stratum, and indeed, for some of them
it is higher than one.

My questions are:

1. Are my estimated of abundace being calculated based on global detection probability?
2. If so, is the model still invalid?

Thanks in advance for your help.

Best,
Ana María.

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] MCDS Warning: detection greater than one
parts:
Ana Maria

It is not possible to answer all of your questions from the information you provided.  But here are a few observations:

- the MCDS engine is the multiple covariate distance sampling engine, permitting the use of covariates in modelling the detection function.  You do not mention what covariates you have included and whether you have allowed adjustment terms to be included along with covariates.  It is common for problems such as yours to arise when adjustment terms are combined with covariates.  Remember, the principle of parsimony is to use the simplest model that provides an adequate explanation to the data.  Ask a) do you need covariates; b) if you need covariates do you also need adjustments.  I suspect the answer to a) is perhaps no and b) almost certainly no.

- I would also not recommend basing the estimate of encounter rate variance upon an *assumption* of Poisson distribution of animals.  This should only be used if there are too few replicate transects to produce an estimation of encounter rate variability from the survey data.

- if you want a detection function that is the same across strata (assuming there is justification for this) and stratum-specific abundance estimates, you would select this arrangement of levels of resolution for estimation of various quantities

messages.author: 7482eee8d2863d12
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] MCDS Warning: detection greater than one
parts:
Further to Eric's response, if you are using covariates in addition to distance
in the detection function, and these covariates are different in different
strata (or are at the sample or observation level), then it makes sense to fit a
global detection function but predict detection probability by stratum, so that
Distance can account for the fact that differences in covariates between strata
will cause differences in detectability between strata.

To do this, in the Estimate tab, under "Quantities to estimate and level of
resolution", in the detection function line, you tick both the Global and
Stratum boxes. (This means estimate a global function, predict by stratum --
for more info see the online help.)

Cheers, Len

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] MCDS Warning: detection greater than one
parts:
Dear Eric and Lean,

thanks for your answers. The solution to the error messege was to remove the option of adjustment terms from all my models. Then all of them, independently of how encounter rate was estimated, run without warning messeges.

Cheers,
Ana
